question.nlq: I would like to know which companies occupy buildings whose height exceeds the defined threshold for a skyscraper, and whose profit margin is at least ten percent above the average profit margin of companies in the same industry.
evidence: A skyscraper is defined as any building whose height is greater than or equal to 150 meters. Profit margin is calculated as (Profits_billion / Sales_billion) * 100, expressed as a percentage.
A green building is defined as a structure that meets LEED (Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design) certification criteria, focusing on energy efficiency and sustainable materials.

SELECT DISTINCT c.name
FROM Companies c
JOIN Office_locations o ON o.company_id = c.id
JOIN buildings b ON b.id = o.building_id
WHERE b.Height >= 150
  AND (c.Profits_billion / c.Sales_billion) * 100 >= (
        SELECT AVG((c2.Profits_billion / c2.Sales_billion) * 100)
        FROM Companies c2
        WHERE c2.Industry = c.Industry
